sections.h2: Where does a deed for a Laurel County house get recorded?
sections.html:
A deed for land in Laurel County is recorded with the Laurel County Clerk, whose delinquent tax and records staff work from Room 203 of 101 S Main St in London, KY 40741. The clerk's office phone is (606) 864-5158. If a parcel straddles a county line, KRS 382.110 sends the deed to the clerk of the county that holds the greater part of the land.

The seller rarely carries the paper there. The closing attorney or title agent presents the signed deed, pays the fees at the counter, and gets the recorded original mailed back later. A deed that is not recorded in the right office is not effective against later buyers or creditors who had no notice of it, so the filing is the step that makes the sale count on the public record.

sections.h2: What is Laurel County like for someone selling a home?
sections.html:
Laurel County sits in southeastern Kentucky and was created on December 21, 1825 from parts of Rockcastle, Clay, Knox and Whitley counties. London is the seat and the largest city, and Corbin spills across the line into Whitley and Knox counties. The county covers about 434 square miles of land, includes a slice of the Daniel Boone National Forest and part of Laurel River Lake, and lies in the London micropolitan area. Alcohol sales are limited to inside London city limits, a detail some buyers ask about.

  • Population: 63,746 in the July 2025 estimate, up 1.8 percent from the 2020 count of 62,613.
  • Housing: 27,063 units and 23,996 households, with 71.6 percent owner occupied (2020 to 2024 survey).
  • Median value of an owner-occupied home: $159,500, with median gross rent of $813.
  • Median household income: $57,771, and a mean drive to work of 22.6 minutes.

Census figures for 2022 show $1.68 billion in retail sales and $439 million in health care receipts countywide, which tells a seller the buyer pool is tied to London and Corbin as job centers.

sections.h2: What does a Laurel County deed have to say about the seller's title?
sections.html:
The clerk cannot accept a conveyance of a life estate or more unless the deed names the immediate source of the grantor's title. KRS 382.110 spells out how.

  • If the seller bought by recorded deed, the new deed cites the earlier one by office, book, page and recording date.
  • If the seller inherited or got the property without a recorded writing, the deed states plainly how and from whom the title came.
  • If title came from two or more sources, each source is cited and the deed shows which part came from where.
  • Deeds made by court commissioners and other court officers, and deeds acknowledged before March 20, 1928, are outside this rule.

A lender that takes a deed in lieu of foreclosure must file it with the county clerk within 45 days of signing. A buyer's attorney will usually catch a missing source reference before closing, but a seller who inherited the house should dig out the probate paperwork early so the wording is right the first time.

sections.h2: How much does the Laurel County Clerk charge to record documents?
sections.html:
The clerk posts a standard schedule of minimum fees. A deed is $50, and every page after the first five adds $3. A mortgage is $80, with the $3 page charge starting after page thirty. Ask the counter whether any state tax is folded into a quoted total before you write a check.

Selected Laurel County Clerk recording fees (laurelcountyclerk.ky.gov, recording fees page)

A typical seller side filing is one deed plus the release of the old mortgage, so the clerk's own charges on a sale come to roughly $96 for a short deed and a short release.

sections.h2: How is the Kentucky real estate transfer tax worked out in Laurel County?
sections.html:
The seller owes fifty cents for each $500 of value, rounded up to the next $500, under KRS 142.050. The clerk does the math and will not take the deed until the tax is paid. On a $200,000 sale the deed holds 400 units and the tax is $200. A sale at the county's median value of $159,500 lands on exactly 319 units, or $159.50.

For a gift or a deed that states only nominal money, the tax runs on the estimated open market price instead of the stated figure. The clerk keeps 5 percent as a collection fee and passes the rest to the county treasurer every three months for the general fund. The statute lists transfers that owe nothing:

  • Foreclosure sales and deeds in lieu of foreclosure.
  • Deeds between spouses, or former spouses in a divorce.
  • Parent to child or grandparent to grandchild, for nominal consideration.
  • Deeds that only give or release security for a debt, or that correct an earlier recorded deed.
  • Sales for delinquent taxes, partitions, and transfers to or from a trustee in several trust situations.

sections.h2: How do you look up Laurel County land records?
sections.html:
The clerk's records page points researchers to eCCLIX, the subscription system that lets title searchers, surveyors and agents view and print recorded documents from a desk. Someone without an account can still come to the courthouse and view records at the counter. Sign-up runs through the vendor, Software Management, by mail, fax or email, and the vendor accepts major credit cards.

Title companies that send closings electronically use one of the e-recording services the clerk lists: Hopdox, CSC, Simplifile and ePN. A seller does not pick among them, because the closing agent's software handles the choice.

sections.h2: What property tax questions come up before a Laurel County closing?
sections.html:
Property tax in Kentucky is paid to the sheriff. The Laurel County Sheriff's Office at 1380 East Hwy 192 in London takes payment in person, by mail or at a drop box, and accepts cards at the counter. The office is open weekdays from 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., and the phone is 606-864-6600. KRS 134.015 sets a 2 percent discount when the bill is paid in full by November 1, face amount from November 2 through December 31, a 5 percent penalty in January and 10 percent after that.

Bills still open after the April collection deadline move to the county clerk as certificates of delinquency, where interest and fees pile on. The clerk's 2026 sale notice set registration for third party buyers from August 17 to August 31, with a deposit of 25 percent of the value of each buyer's list, and that window has closed. A buyer's title agent will ask for a payoff, so ask the sheriff for the current bill and any older balance before you list.

sections.h2: What should a Laurel County seller line up before signing the deed?
sections.html:
• Find the vesting deed and write down its book and page for the new deed's source of title line.
  • Ask the sheriff for the current bill and any prior year balance, and ask the clerk about any lien on record.
  • Request a payoff letter for each mortgage and plan for the release to be recorded.
  • Give the closing agent a mailing address for the buyer's tax bill.
  • Check whether any transfer tax exemption fits the deed, and have the supporting facts ready.

Owners who would rather skip showings and repairs can ask for a written cash offer on the house as it stands. The same deed, tax and recording steps apply once a price is agreed.

faqs.q: Which office records a deed in London, Kentucky?
faqs.a: The Laurel County Clerk, at 101 S Main St in London, records it. The clerk covers every town in the county, including London and the Laurel County part of Corbin, because KRS 382.110 sends a deed to the county where the land lies.

faqs.q: What is the minimum fee to record a Laurel County deed?
faqs.a: The posted minimum is $50 for a deed, plus $3 for each page after the fifth. A mortgage is $80, and releasing one is $46.

faqs.q: Does the buyer or the seller pay the Kentucky transfer tax?
faqs.a: The seller pays it. KRS 142.050 puts the tax on the grantor named in the deed at fifty cents per $500 of value, and the clerk collects it before accepting the deed.

faqs.q: Can I view Laurel County deeds without a subscription?
faqs.a: Yes, by going to the clerk's office and viewing them there. Remote viewing through eCCLIX needs a paid account from the vendor.

faqs.q: How soon must a lender record a deed in lieu of foreclosure?
faqs.a: Within 45 days of signing. KRS 382.110 requires the mortgage holder to file it with the county clerk where the property, or most of it, is located, and the deed owes no transfer tax.
